texts.preamble: Shri Velu vs Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd on 20 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This the 20th day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.6426/2017 Petitioner Shri Velu, Son of Arjun, Aged about 32 years, No.28, 2nd Cross, Krishnananda Nagar, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru-560 096. (By Pleader Shri B.R.Srinath) V/s. Respondents 1.Tata Aig General Insurance Co. Ltd., 2nd floor, No.69, Miller's Road, Bengaluru-560 052. Policy No.015749423600 valid from 12.9.2017 to 11.9.2018. Car No.KA-04-MN-3369. (By Pleader Shri V.Muralidhara) 2 Scch-18 Mvc 6426/2017 2.M/s Bengaluru Medical Systems Ltd., Bms House No.38, Lakshmaiah Block, Ganganagar, Bengaluru-560 032 . (By Pleader Shri D.Harish) J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.3,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 20.9.2017 at about 3.20 p.m. the petitioner was pushing his cart on MEI Factory road carefully and cautiously, when he reached near RMC Yard, 6th Gate Junction, at that time a car bearing No.KA-04-3369 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner. Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately he was shifted to K.C.General Hospital, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru wherein he took the treatment as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 47 years, doing a coolie and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-04-MN-3369. Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared before the court and inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.2 has not filed his written statement. So, the written statement of the respondent No.2 is taken as not filed. The respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further this respondent has denied about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-03-MN- 3369 and its validity. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 has not led any evidence on its behalf.
texts.arguments: Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same. Further contended that the accident occurred due to the carelessness on the part of the petitioner himself. During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has denied the accident in toto, hence, prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.1. On the other hand, petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 24. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 47 years, coolie and getting an income of Rs.15,000/- per month. Due to the accident he is unable to walk for long distance, cannot bear weight on his right leg, cannot climb stairs and often gets pain in his right leg. The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability. The petitioner has produced x-ray at Ex.P9. Therefore, no amount is granted under this head. 25. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained fractures.
